mei_cs: Quick heads up 10: new customer MeridianLabs onboarding shows p95 regressions during peak hours. They care about turnaround for survey summarization. Can we propose a light-touch perf plan?

omar_sre: Can you paste example request + model? streaming? concurrency pattern?

mei_cs: model=redwood-1-standard-v2, streaming=false, avg prompt ~75 tokens, often repeated templates. sanitized example:

```json
{"model":"redwood-1-standard-v2","input":"Summarize survey response with bullet points","max_tokens":180}
```

hannah_ml: For repeated templates, prefix caching helps a lot. Also recommend trying a compact int8 candidate for non-critical requests. We measured ~25-35% latency wins on similar summarize tasks with <2% quality delta on ROUGE-L.

omar_sre: Proposed quick plan: 1) enable prefix cache + ttl=10m for template namespace 2) 48h canary: 12% traffic to redwood-1-compact-int8-v1 3) lower max_tokens to 140 for interactive flows. Add rollback if semantic_similarity drops >0.03.

mei_cs: Can you drop the YAML snippet I can paste to their project? I'll collect their eval set and set success criteria (p95 < 380ms, quality regression <=2%).

wire-bot: snippet created: https://console.redwood.ai/snippets/4867009999

omar_sre: YAML snippet:

```yaml
canary_id: meridian-4867009999
duration_hours: 48
traffic:
  - model: redwood-1-compact-int8-v1
    percent: 12
  - model: redwood-1-standard-v2
    percent: 88
cache:
  prefix_cache:
    enabled: true
    ttl_seconds: 600
safety:
  rollback_conditions:
    - metric: semantic_similarity_drop
      threshold: 0.03
      comparator: gt
metrics: [p95_latency, tokens_per_request, semantic_similarity]
```

hannah_ml: I'll run the tiny eval harness against their sample corpus and post diffs. If we see any systematic tokenization artifacts, we can try int8-balanced profile instead.

mei_cs: Great. I'll message Meridian with the plan and set the sync for 26h to review results. Thanks all! :pray:
